A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NCTTA work, and all 10 pages of each are readable. However, both reference Appendices A–C that are absent from the supplied files, limiting comparison of proofs, detailed settings, and supplementary results.

before.justification: V1 reports original NCTTA benchmark results in Tables 1–6, alongside empirical neural-collapse validation, ablations, and feature-alignment analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and analytical experiments, including revised numerical results in several tables.

M1.justification: Equation 7 replaces exp(-d/epsilon) with a softmax of negative Z-score-normalized distances before blending with predictive probabilities. This changes the relative weighting and potentially the selected hybrid targets, while retaining the alignment losses, entropy filtering, and adaptive weighting framework.

E1.justification: The supplied material retains ImageNet-100 validation and evaluations on CIFAR-10-C, ImageNet-C, PACS, and Waterbirds, with mild shifts, continual adaptation, and batch-size-one scenarios. Both versions also describe CIFAR-100-C evaluation but defer its results to the missing Appendix C. No coverage addition is established.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the displayed tables is unchanged. V2 newly states that appendix results compare EATA-C, SAR², COME, and AdaDEM on CIFAR-10/100-C and ImageNet-C. Because that appendix is absent, their participation and comparison scope cannot be verified.

E3.justification: Visible settings retain ResNet50/ViT-B/16 backbones, TTAB defaults, corruption severities, batch-size-one testing, and loss-comparison settings. Detailed configurations remain deferred to the missing Appendix B.2, and protocols for the newly advertised baseline comparisons are unavailable, preventing a complete assessment.

E4.justification: Table 4 revises the component-ablation evidence while retaining the same configurations and questions. Full-model accuracies change from 78.51/66.39 to 78.10/66.50 on CIFAR-10-C/ImageNet-C, with partial-variant results also revised. The loss-form, target-sensitivity, and geometric analyses retain their scope and conclusions.

E5.justification: The supplied pages retain the same use of ± uncertainty entries and point-estimate tables. Changed uncertainty values accompany revised results, but no new reporting practice, run-count disclosure, confidence interval, or significance test appears.

E6.justification: NCTTA averages change from 78.51 to 78.16 and 66.39 to 66.46 in Table 1, 76.77 to 77.36 on PACS, 71.32 to 71.27 for continual adaptation, and 59.55 to 59.69 for batch size one. Table 4 also changes; Waterbirds results remain identical. These are revised results accompanying the method modification, with leading average rankings retained.

T1.justification: Equation 7 substantively revises the mathematical definition of the hybrid score through distance standardization and probability normalization. The FCA definitions and NC3+ convergence statement remain unchanged; replacing 'Theorem' with 'Proposition' is only a label change. The referenced Appendix A.3 proof is unavailable in both files.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of sample-wise neural collapse, misalignment as the explanation for degradation, hybrid-target alignment, and broad adaptation effectiveness. The headline performance claims are also retained despite updates to corresponding tables.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning misalignment, unreliable pseudo-labels, component complementarity, and improved feature clustering remain the same. Both retain the limitations concerning class-prototype learning in mini-batches and extension to vision-language models; additional citations do not change these boundaries.

D1.justification: V2 adds a public project/repository link in the abstract, providing an access pointer absent from v1. Its contents and availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Detailed implementation and hyperparameter information remains delegated to missing appendices.

R1.justification: V2 adds nine bibliography entries, including CLiFF, MoETTA, COSMIC, and the four newly named supplementary comparators. These broaden the cited TTA and vision-language literature, while the related-work organization and claimed relationship between neural collapse and TTA remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 updates affiliation and contact information, adds acknowledgments, expands the explanation surrounding Equation 7, and makes localized terminology edits. The main section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 moves Figure 2 from page 3 to page 4, adjusts graphic sizes and placement, adds an 'Avg. Acc.' axis label to Figure 6(a), and reflows the text and references. The inventory of eight figures and six tables is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds an access pointer and documents a normalized hybrid-target calculation, but its quality benefit is not established. Reporting consistency worsens: Section 5.2 still quotes 71.32% and 59.55%, whereas Tables 5 and 6 now report 71.27% and 59.69%. The newly advertised baseline comparisons cannot be checked because the appendices are missing. These documentation gains, new inconsistencies, and unavailable supporting evidence prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
